Sedentary

SED-un-tair-ee -- Latin sedere, 'to sit': a sedentary life is a sitting life. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Sedentary is involving much sitting and little physical activity.

Worried about his sedentary desk job, Omar started biking to the office twice a week.

Worked Example

A software tester's smartwatch buzzes at 4 p.m. with a gentle reminder: in seven hours, he has taken exactly 212 steps, all of them between his desk and the coffee machine.

A routine spent almost entirely sitting still is exactly what sedentary describes. Unlike 'lazy,' which judges someone's character, sedentary neutrally describes a lack of physical movement.

How Sedentary Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

inactive

inactive: not physically active

immobile

immobile: not moving at all

desk-bound

desk-bound: kept sitting at a desk for long hours

Antonyms

active

active: physically energetic and moving often

mobile

mobile: moving or able to move about easily

How Strong Is It? — inactive → sedentary → immobile

inactive vs. sedentary

inactive vs. sedentary: Inactive is the plain, general cousin of sedentary -- inactive just means not moving much, while sedentary specifically pictures a life organized around sitting.

immobile vs. sedentary

immobile vs. sedentary: Immobile is more extreme than sedentary: a sedentary person still walks around, just not much, while immobile means barely able to move at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — sed-

root — sed-: to sit (Latin (sedere))

suffix — -entary

suffix — -entary: relating to, characterized by (Latin (-arius))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin sedentarius meant 'sitting' -- from sedere, 'to sit' -- so a sedentary job is literally a sitting job, the same root that gives us sediment, the material that sits at the bottom of a lake.

Root Check

Word Choice

Sedentary most often modifies 'lifestyle,' 'job,' or 'work,' describing physical inactivity -- it comments on how much a body moves, not on how hard a person works.
